intro: Arkansas Legislative Audit examines every county and publishes what it finds. This page quotes what the auditors reported about Clay County, from its latest report — no verdict added in either direction. What the auditors said is the record; what to make of it is yours.
regulatory_basis_note: Read this before reading any Arkansas audit: county and city reports carry a technical 'adverse opinion' on GAAP grounds because Arkansas law has them keep books on a simpler 'regulatory basis.' That phrase appears in every such audit in the state and signals the accounting format — not wrongdoing. A report is 'clean' or not in its findings, deficiencies, and noncompliance sections, which is what this page quotes.

verdicts.quote: Noncompliance with state law and accepted accounting practices was noted in the office of Sheriff and Tax Collector. Sheriff and Tax Collector The following deficiencies were noted during the review of the Sheriff's Commissary account: • Bank reconciliations were not performed in noncompliance with Ark. Code Ann. §14-25-107.
verdicts.detail: A limited review (a “financial and compliance report”), not a full audit: the financial statements in it are unaudited. The letter continues in the report on page 3; parts that concern staff positions are left to the report, since this site doesn’t single out non-elected staff.

limits: From the 2024 report, dated October 1, 2025. Read by machine from the report’s text; the quotes are the auditors’ words. Older reports, and the separate federal (single) audits, aren’t on this page yet.
Arkansas alternates between full audits and limited “financial and compliance” reviews; each line says which this is.

cities.quote: Noncompliance with state law and accepted accounting practices was noted in the office of Recorder/Treasurer. Recorder/Treasurer Compensation paid to an elected official was reported to the Internal Revenue Service (IRS) on Form 1099-NEC instead of Form W-2. A similar finding was noted in the previous report.

cities.name: Pollard
cities.quote: Noncompliance with state law and accepted accounting practices was noted in the office of Recorder/Treasurer. Recorder/Treasurer A review of the City's 2025 payroll records revealed Internal Revenue Service (IRS) quarterly 941 reports were not prepared or submitted in 2025, and the City did not remit payroll withholdings for 2025. Because the City has not received any correspondence from the IRS, we were unable to determine the total amount owed by the City, including any potential penalties and interest.
